subject: Integration & Observability - SDK auth, routing, and trace headers
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@fintechco.com>, FintechCo Engineering <engineering@fintechco.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Integration & Observability - SDK auth, routing, and trace headers

Hi Alex / team,

Thanks again for taking the call today — appreciate the deep dive on your payments flow and the A/B reranking use case. Below is a short recap and proposed next steps so we can move the technical handoff to your engineering team:

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary integration: server-side inference calls from your transaction-service (Node.js / TypeScript) for both generation (structured tool-calling output) and embeddings-based reranking.
- Auth: Prefer short-lived tokens from your internal auth service (OIDC) and want support for scoped API keys per environment.
- Routing & HA: Need region-aware routing (primary us-west, fallback us-east) and automated fallback to a cheaper model variant under capacity pressure.
- Observability: Critical — you want trace ID propagation, per-request token-level latency breakdown, and request/response headers showing routing/queueing latency. Also a pre-built dashboard for per-route P50/P95, cost per 1k tokens, and sampling of model outputs for drift detection.

Integration notes/actions (what we propose)
1) SDK & auth
   - Use our Node SDK (examples attached). SDK supports OIDC short-lived tokens and environment-scoped API keys.
   - Recommend token refresh TTL = 5m for high-throughput services; we support JWT audiences and token introspection if you prefer.
2) Structured output & tool-calling
   - We recommend using the Structured Responses API to enforce JSON schema. SDK includes validators and deterministic tool-calling hooks.
3) Embeddings & reranker
   - Store embeddings in your vector DB (we integrate with Pinecone/FAISS). Reranker can be run as an additional scoring step; we recommend batching queries (batch size ~64) for throughput.
4) Observability hooks (priority for this handoff)
   - Trace IDs: propagate your trace-id header (traceparent or x-trace-id) through the SDK; Redwood will echo the header back and include it in logs.
   - Latency headers: responses include X-Redwood-Latency (total ms) and X-Redwood-Breakdown (queue:exec:network in ms).
   - Logging fields: request_id, model_version, route_id, cpu_ms, gpu_ms, token_count, reranker_score_sample.
   - Dashboard: we'll share a dashboard template (link below) and a perf template with examples of P50/P95 and per-route cost.

Attachments: integration-observability-checklist.pdf (application/pdf, 420KB stub)

Proposed next steps
- Rishi (cc'd) from our solutions team to run a 60-min technical session with your engineers next week.
- Please confirm the preferred auth approach (OIDC short-lived tokens vs scoped API keys) and availability windows (we suggested Wed/Thu 10:00-13:00 PT).

Thanks — I’ll loop Rishi in next for the tech details.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

2) SDKs: Node.js is primary, but we have a small Python ML service that will call the reranker. Can you share the minimal code snippet (auth + call + handling of X-Redwood-Breakdown header)?
3) Embeddings: retention policy — we need to retain embeddings for 13 months for audit; any export/ingest recommendations?
4) Observability: can you provide the exact header names and an example of the X-Redwood-Breakdown value? Also, we'd like your dashboard JSON so we can import into Grafana and tie to our traces.

We're generally aligned on routing fallback; one ask: if you fall back to cheaper variants, can you include the model_version in the response headers so we can correlate quality regressions?

Alex / Marissa — thanks, happy to run the tech session Wed 22 Jul 10:30 PT. Below are quick answers and a minimal snippet — I attached sdk-snippets.zip with runnable examples and a Grafana dashboard JSON (dashboard-import.json).

Quick answers:
- Token introspection: yes — SDK supports verifying token active state via introspection endpoint. We also support validating JWKS and audience claim.
- Header names: 
   * Trace propagation: prefer standard traceparent; SDK will forward traceparent and populate logs with trace_id.
   * Latency headers: X-Redwood-Latency: total_ms; X-Redwood-Breakdown: queue:exec:network (example "12:85:5" in ms).
   * Model version header: X-Redwood-Model-Version (e.g., "redwood-v2.3-quant")
- Embeddings retention: we recommend exporting periodically to your object store (S3) via our export job; retention can be handled in your vector DB lifecycle policies. We include metadata (created_at, source_id) for audit.
- Reranker throughput: recommend batching (64-128) and async workers. Expect ~1200 qps per p3.8xlarge equivalent for small vectors; we'll validate on the tech call with your sample traffic.

Minimal Node snippet (auth + call + parse breakdown header):

const { RedwoodClient } = require('@redwood/sdk');
const client = new RedwoodClient({ baseURL: 'https://api.redwood.com', tokenProvider: async () => await fetchToken() });

async function score(input) {
  const res = await client.requests.create({ route: 'reranker', model: 'redwood-rerank-v1', input });
  console.log('X-Redwood-Latency:', res.headers['x-redwood-latency']);
  console.log('X-Redwood-Breakdown:', res.headers['x-redwood-breakdown']); // e.g. "12:85:5"
  console.log('X-Redwood-Model-Version:', res.headers['x-redwood-model-version']);
  return res.data;
}

Handling structured output/tool-calling: use the structured_response flag and schema in the request. SDK will validate and surface tool calls as an object on the response.

Grafana dashboard: attached dashboard-import.json — includes panels for per-route P50/P95 latency, token_cost_per_1k, model_version distribution, and sample output snapshots (sampling = 1%).

Next steps:
- Tech session Wed 22 Jul 10:30 PT (calendar invite forthcoming).
- After session: follow-up with a PoC checklist and sample ingestion job for embeddings export.

If you want, I can also join your infra office hours later this week to validate network egress rules for short-lived token introspection endpoints.
